rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.
Prepending a backslash to an ordinary character in a string does not have any effect, and may make regular expressions constructed from this string behave unexpectedly.

If two functions with the same name are declared in the same scope, one of the declarations overrides the other without warning. This makes the code hard to read and maintain, and may even lead to platform-dependent behavior.
Sensitive cookies set by a server can be read by the client if the `httpOnly` flag is not set.
The 'eval' function and the 'Function' constructor execute strings as code. This is dangerous and impedes program analysis and understanding. Consequently, these two functions should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
rules.description: Memory operations access outside the intended buffer boundary.
The Helmet middleware is used to set security-related HTTP headers in Express applications. This query finds instances where the middleware is configured with important security features disabled.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
rules.description: If the 'X-Frame-Options' setting is not provided, a malicious user may be able to overlay their own UI on top of the site by using an iframe.
The body of a control statement should have appropriate indentation to clarify which statements it controls and which ones it does not control.
Storing unencrypted passwords in configuration files is unsafe.
